breakfast.name: Fattah (Bread and Egg)
instructions: Tear flatbread into bowl
Scramble eggs with butter
Pour over bread
Drizzle with honey, sprinkle black seed
breakfast.description: Bread soaked with scrambled egg and honey.

breakfast.name: Malawach (Fried Flatbread)
instructions: Make dough, rest
Layer with butter, fold repeatedly
Roll thin, fry in pan until golden
Serve with eggs and zhug
breakfast.description: Flaky, buttery fried flatbread — Yemeni-Jewish origin.

breakfast.name: Jachnun (Slow-Baked Rolled Dough)
instructions: Jachnun is the Yemeni-Jewish Shabbat breakfast -- dough rolled thin and baked overnight
Thin sheets of dough brushed with butter or margarine, rolled tightly
Placed in a pot and baked on very low heat for 10-12 hours (overnight)
The result: a dark, caramelized, flaky pastry -- deeply sweet from the long slow baking
The Maillard reaction over 12 hours transforms the simple dough
Eggs placed in the pot alongside turn brown from the long cooking -- "haminados" eggs
Brought to Israel by Yemeni Jews (the Teimanim) during mass immigration in the 1940s-50s
Now one of Israel's most popular Shabbat morning foods -- but its origin is Yemeni
Served with grated tomato relish and schug (spicy green chili paste)
breakfast.description: Yemeni-Jewish Shabbat pastry -- jachnun, thin buttered dough rolled tight and baked on low heat for 10-12 hours overnight. The slow Maillard reaction turns it dark, caramelized, and deeply sweet. Eggs cooked alongside turn brown (haminados). Brought to Israel by Yemeni Jews in the 1940s-50s. Served with tomato relish and schug.

breakfast.name: Lahoh (Yemeni Pancake)
instructions: Lahoh is the Yemeni spongy pancake -- similar to Ethiopian injera but smaller and thicker
A yeast-fermented batter cooked on one side only until the top is covered in bubbles
Spongy and porous -- designed to absorb sauces and stews
Eaten for breakfast with honey or with savory dishes (beans, eggs)
The Yemeni connection to the Horn of Africa: lahoh is also made in Djibouti and Somalia
Yemen and the Horn of Africa are separated by the narrow Bab al-Mandab strait -- cuisines intertwine
breakfast.description: Yemeni spongy pancake -- lahoh, fermented batter cooked on one side until bubbly and porous. Similar to Ethiopian injera but smaller and thicker. Eaten with honey or savory stews. Yemen and the Horn of Africa (Djibouti, Somalia) share this bread across the narrow Bab al-Mandab strait.

breakfast.name: Ful Medames (Fava Beans)
ingredients: Fava beans (dried, soaked overnight, or canned)
instructions: Ful medames is the fava bean dish eaten across the Arab world and the Horn of Africa
Slow-cooked fava beans mashed and seasoned with olive oil, lemon, garlic, and cumin
A protein-rich breakfast -- the working person's morning fuel
Variations across the region: Egyptian ful uses tahini, Yemeni ful uses more cumin and chili
Eaten with bread for scooping -- no utensils needed
One of the oldest prepared foods in the world -- fava beans have been cultivated for 8,000+ years
breakfast.description: Ancient Arab breakfast -- ful medames, slow-cooked fava beans mashed with olive oil, lemon, garlic, and cumin. A protein-rich morning fuel eaten with bread. Fava beans have been cultivated for 8,000+ years. Variations across the Arab world: Yemeni ful uses more cumin and chili.

lunch.name: Saltah
instructions: Make meat broth with vegetables
Make sahawiq paste
Whip hilbeh foam from fenugreek
Serve in stone bowl: broth, sahawiq, hilbeh on top
Eat with flatbread
lunch.description: Yemen's national dish — hot stone pot of broth, chili, and fenugreek foam.

lunch.name: Mandi (Meat and Rice)
instructions: Season lamb with hawaij
Slow-roast or smoke in tandoor 2 hours
Cook rice in meat drippings with spices
Serve rice topped with tender meat

lunch.name: Zorbian (Yemeni Biryani)
ingredients: Hawaij spice (Yemeni spice blend: cumin, cardamom, turmeric, black pepper, coriander)
instructions: Zorbian is the Yemeni biryani -- a layered rice dish with Indian Ocean trade influence
The Yemeni version of biryani: rice layered with spiced meat and baked
Hawaij: the Yemeni spice blend that distinguishes this from Indian biryani
The Indian Ocean spice trade connected Yemen to India for millennia
Aden (Yemen's port city) was a major trading hub -- Indian, African, and Arab cuisines mixed
The rice is partially cooked, layered with the meat, and steamed until the flavors meld
Served with a tomato-chili sauce on the side
lunch.description: Yemeni layered rice -- zorbian, basmati rice layered with spiced chicken or lamb, fried onions, and hawaij (Yemeni spice blend). Indian Ocean trade connected Yemen to India for millennia. Aden was a major trading hub where Indian, African, and Arab cuisines mixed. Served with tomato-chili sauce.

lunch.name: Haneeth (Slow-Roasted Lamb)
instructions: Haneeth is the Yemeni slow-roasted lamb -- cooked in a tandoor (taboun) oven
Lamb rubbed with hawaij spice and salt, slow-roasted for 4-6 hours
The tandoor (taboun): a clay oven heated by burning wood at the bottom
The lamb emerges fall-apart tender, deeply spiced, and smoky
Similar to mandi but with a different spice profile and cooking technique
Served on a bed of spiced rice
A celebration dish -- weddings, Eid, and large gatherings
Yemeni lamb traditions are among the oldest in the Arabian Peninsula
lunch.description: Yemeni slow-roasted lamb -- haneeth, whole lamb rubbed with hawaij spice and roasted 4-6 hours in a taboun (clay oven). Fall-apart tender, deeply spiced, and smoky. Served on spiced rice. For weddings and Eid celebrations. Among the oldest Arabian Peninsula lamb traditions.

lunch.name: Shafout (Flatbread in Yoghurt)
instructions: Shafout is the Yemeni flatbread soaked in seasoned yoghurt -- a cooling summer dish
Flatbread torn and soaked in garlicky, spiced yoghurt
The bread softens and absorbs the tangy yoghurt
A refreshing dish for hot Yemeni summers
Simple and quick -- uses leftover bread
The yoghurt-and-bread combination is ancient -- found across the Middle East and Central Asia
lunch.description: Yemeni flatbread in yoghurt -- shafout, torn lahoh or malawach soaked in garlicky, cumin-spiced yoghurt. A cooling summer dish. Simple and ancient -- the yoghurt-and-bread combination exists across the Middle East and Central Asia. Uses leftover bread.

lunch.name: Kabsa (Spiced Rice with Chicken)
instructions: Kabsa is the Arabian spiced rice dish -- shared across Yemen, Saudi Arabia, and the Gulf
Chicken or lamb cooked with spices and tomato, the rice cooked in the flavored broth
Hawaij and loomi (dried black lime) give the Yemeni accent
Loomi: the same sour dried lime used across the Gulf -- boiled and sun-dried until black
A one-pot rice dish: the meat broth flavors the rice as they cook together
Kabsa is everyday lunch food across the Arabian Peninsula
lunch.description: Arabian spiced rice -- kabsa, chicken cooked with hawaij spice and loomi (dried black lime), rice cooked in the flavored broth. Shared across Yemen, Saudi Arabia, and the Gulf. Hawaij and loomi give the Yemeni accent. Everyday lunch across the Arabian Peninsula.

lunch.name: Fatteh (Bread, Chickpeas, and Yoghurt)
instructions: Fatteh is the Yemeni and Levantine layered dish -- bread, chickpeas, and yoghurt
Toasted bread at the bottom soaks up the garlicky yoghurt and chickpea cooking liquid
Topped with yoghurt, tahini, and toasted pine nuts
An ancient dish -- using stale bread as a base is the resourceful cooking of the Arab world
The layers: bread absorbs, chickpeas provide protein, yoghurt provides tang and richness
A hearty lunch or brunch dish
lunch.description: Yemeni and Levantine layered dish -- fatteh, toasted flatbread soaked in chickpea broth, topped with garlicky yoghurt, tahini, and toasted pine nuts. Resourceful cooking: stale bread becomes the base. The layers provide texture, protein, and tang.

dinner.name: Fahsa (Meat Stew)
instructions: Brown lamb in ghee
Add onion, garlic, tomatoes
Add hawaij and water, simmer 35 min
Top with fenugreek foam
Serve in stone pot with bread
dinner.description: Lamb stew with fenugreek — served in a hot stone bowl.

dinner.name: Aseed (Flour Porridge)
instructions: Cook flour with water into thick, smooth paste
Shape into mound
Pour lamb broth or honey over
dinner.description: Dense flour porridge — sweet or savory.

dinner.name: Shakshouka (Eggs in Tomato Sauce)
ingredients: Tomato sauce (tomatoes, onion, garlic, bell pepper)
instructions: Shakshouka is the eggs poached in spiced tomato sauce -- a dish shared across the Arab world and North Africa
The Yemeni version is spicier than the Tunisian or Israeli versions
Eggs cracked directly into a simmering tomato-pepper sauce in a skillet
The eggs cook in the sauce -- the whites set while the yolks stay runny
Eaten directly from the skillet with bread for dipping into the sauce and breaking the yolks
The name may come from the Arabic word for "mixture"
A dinner or breakfast dish -- versatile and quick
dinner.description: Eggs poached in spiced tomato sauce -- shakshouka, eggs cracked into a simmering skillet of tomato-pepper sauce with cumin and chili. Yolks stay runny. Eaten from the skillet with bread. The Yemeni version is spicier than Tunisian or Israeli versions.

dinner.name: Ogda (Meat and Vegetable Stew)
instructions: Ogda is the Yemeni meat and vegetable stew -- a rustic one-pot dinner
Chunks of meat simmered with vegetables in a spiced broth
Topped with hulba: whipped fenugreek foam -- the essential Yemeni condiment
Hulba: fenugreek seeds soaked, then whipped into a frothy, slightly bitter foam
Fenugreek is central to Yemeni cuisine -- more than any other Arab cuisine
A home-cooked dinner -- everyday Yemeni food
dinner.description: Yemeni rustic stew -- ogda, lamb and vegetables simmered in a hawaij-spiced broth, topped with hulba (whipped fenugreek foam -- the essential Yemeni condiment). Fenugreek is more central to Yemeni cuisine than any other Arab cuisine. Everyday home cooking.

dinner.name: Zurbiyan (Festive Rice with Meat)
instructions: Zurbiyan is the Yemeni festive layered rice -- made for celebrations and large gatherings
Lamb cooked in a spiced broth, rice partially cooked, both layered in a pot
Fried potato slices line the bottom -- they become crispy and caramelized (the tahdig equivalent)
The pot is sealed and steamed so the flavors meld
Flipped upside down to serve -- the crispy potatoes are on top
A maqluba-like presentation -- dramatic and generous
Served at weddings, Eid al-Adha, and major celebrations
dinner.description: Yemeni festive layered rice -- zurbiyan, lamb and rice layered over fried potato slices, sealed and steamed, then flipped upside down (crispy potatoes on top). Dramatic maqluba-like presentation. For weddings and Eid al-Adha celebrations. Saffron, hawaij, and caramelized onions.

dinner.name: Maraq (Yemeni Bone Broth Soup)
instructions: Maraq is the Yemeni bone broth soup -- clear, spiced, and deeply nourishing
Bones simmered for 2+ hours until the marrow dissolves into the broth
Seasoned with hawaij -- the ever-present Yemeni spice blend
Topped with hulba (whipped fenugreek foam)
Drunk from a bowl or eaten with bread
Considered restorative -- given to the sick and to new mothers
The Yemeni grandmother's remedy for everything
dinner.description: Yemeni bone broth -- maraq, lamb or beef bones simmered 2+ hours until marrow dissolves, seasoned with hawaij, topped with hulba (whipped fenugreek foam). Considered restorative -- given to the sick and new mothers. The Yemeni grandmother's remedy for everything.

snacks.name: Bint al-Sahn (Honey Cake)
instructions: Make soft dough with lots of butter
Layer thin sheets in pan
Bake at 175°C 20 min
Drizzle generously with honey
Eat by tearing with hands
snacks.description: Buttery layered pastry drowned in honey — served before the meal.

snacks.name: Sambousek (Fried Pastries)
ingredients: Filling: spiced ground meat with onion, or cheese and herb
instructions: Yemeni sambousek are fried pastries -- part of the pan-Islamic samosa family
Thin pastry folded around spiced meat or cheese
Deep-fried until crispy and golden
A Ramadan iftar staple -- eaten when breaking the fast
The samosa family stretches from India (samosa) through Central Asia (samsa) to the Arab world (sambousek)
Small, portable, and satisfying
snacks.description: Yemeni fried pastries -- sambousek, thin dough around spiced meat or cheese, deep-fried golden. A Ramadan iftar staple. Part of the samosa family stretching from India through Central Asia to the Arab world.

snacks.name: Schug (Spicy Chili Paste)
instructions: Schug (also zhug or sahawiq) is the Yemeni green chili paste -- fiery and herbal
Fresh green chilies blended with cilantro, garlic, and spices
Intensely spicy -- Yemeni food is among the spiciest in the Arab world
Used as a condiment with everything: bread, rice, meat, eggs
Brought to Israel by Yemeni Jews -- now ubiquitous in Israeli cuisine
Green schug (most common) and red schug (with red peppers, less cilantro)
The cilantro is as important as the chili -- it provides the herbal freshness
snacks.description: Yemeni fiery green chili paste -- schug (zhug), fresh green chilies blended with cilantro, garlic, cumin, and cardamom. Intensely spicy -- Yemeni food is among the spiciest in the Arab world. Brought to Israel by Yemeni Jews. The cilantro provides herbal freshness alongside the heat.

snacks.name: Kubaneh (Overnight Bread)
instructions: Kubaneh is the Yemeni-Jewish Shabbat bread -- baked overnight like jachnun
A pull-apart bread: dough divided into balls, each brushed with butter, arranged in a pot
Baked on very low heat overnight -- 8+ hours
The result: soft, rich, buttery bread with a slightly caramelized bottom
Eaten on Shabbat morning with hard-boiled eggs (haminados), grated tomato, and schug
The Yemeni-Jewish culinary tradition is one of the oldest Jewish food traditions in the world
Yemeni Jews (Teimanim) lived in Yemen for over 2,000 years before their mass emigration to Israel
snacks.description: Yemeni-Jewish Shabbat bread -- kubaneh, butter-brushed dough balls baked overnight (8+ hours) on low heat until soft, rich, and caramelized. Eaten Shabbat morning with haminados eggs, tomato, and schug. The Teimanim (Yemeni Jews) lived in Yemen for 2,000+ years. One of the oldest Jewish food traditions.

snacks.name: Basbousa (Semolina Sweet)
instructions: Basbousa is the semolina sweet cake found across the Arab world
A dense semolina batter baked and soaked in orange blossom syrup
Cut into diamond or square pieces, each topped with an almond
Sweet, syrupy, and fragrant
An everyday sweet bought from bakeries
The same dessert family as rawani -- semolina-syrup cakes span the Arab and Ottoman worlds
snacks.description: Arab semolina sweet -- basbousa, dense semolina cake baked and soaked in orange blossom syrup, topped with almonds and cut into diamonds. An everyday bakery sweet across the Arab world.

desserts.name: Masoub (Banana Bread Pudding)
instructions: Crumble bread
Mash bananas, mix with bread
Add cream and honey
Top with black seed
desserts.description: Mashed banana and bread with cream and honey.

desserts.name: Rawani (Semolina Cake)
ingredients: Sugar syrup (scented with rosewater or orange blossom)
instructions: Rawani is the Yemeni semolina cake soaked in scented syrup
A dense semolina batter baked until golden
Hot sugar syrup (rosewater or orange blossom scented) poured over the warm cake
The cake absorbs the syrup and becomes moist and fragrant
Similar to basbousa (Egyptian) and revani (Turkish) -- the semolina-syrup cake tradition spans the Middle East and Ottoman world
Topped with almonds and cut into diamond shapes
desserts.description: Yemeni semolina cake -- rawani, dense semolina batter baked golden and soaked in rosewater-scented sugar syrup. Similar to basbousa and revani across the Middle East. The semolina-syrup cake tradition spans the Ottoman world. Topped with almonds, cut into diamonds.

desserts.name: Sabia (Yemeni Custard)
instructions: Sabia is the Yemeni milk custard -- set with cornstarch and flavored with cardamom and saffron
Milk thickened with cornstarch and sweetened, flavored with Arabian aromatics
Poured into bowls to set
Garnished with crushed pistachios and almonds
Similar to muhallabia across the Arab world
A light, fragrant dessert served after heavy meals
desserts.description: Yemeni milk custard -- sabia, milk thickened with cornstarch, flavored with cardamom, saffron, and rosewater. Garnished with pistachios and almonds. Similar to muhallabia across the Arab world. A light, fragrant dessert after heavy meals.

desserts.name: Luqmat al-Qadi (Yemeni Doughnuts)
instructions: Luqmat al-qadi are Yemeni fried doughnut balls -- "the judge's morsels"
Yeast batter dropped into hot oil and fried until golden
Immediately soaked in sugar syrup or honey
Crispy outside, soft and airy inside, syrupy throughout
Similar to luqaimat (UAE/Gulf), loukoumades (Greek), and zalabia across the Arab world
The name "judge's morsels" -- perhaps because they were sweet enough to bribe a judge
A Ramadan sweet -- eaten at iftar
desserts.description: Yemeni fried doughnut balls -- luqmat al-qadi (the judge's morsels -- sweet enough to bribe a judge), yeast batter fried golden and soaked in honey or sugar syrup. Crispy outside, airy inside. A Ramadan iftar sweet. Part of the pan-Arab luqaimat/loukoumades family.

desserts.name: Halwa (Yemeni Sweet Confection)
instructions: Yemeni halwa is the dense, aromatic sweet confection -- different from Indian or Turkish halva
Flour or semolina cooked in generous ghee with sugar and aromatics
Flavored with cardamom, saffron, and rosewater -- the Arabian sweet spice trinity
Rich, dense, and served in small portions because of the intensity
A Ramadan sweet and celebration confection
Yemeni halwa is especially rich in ghee -- almost candy-like in its density
desserts.description: Yemeni aromatic confection -- halwa, flour or semolina cooked in generous ghee with sugar, cardamom, saffron, and rosewater. Dense and intensely rich. Served in small portions. A Ramadan and celebration sweet. The Arabian sweet spice trinity: cardamom, saffron, rosewater.

drinks.name: Qishr (Coffee Husk Tea)
instructions: Boil husks with ginger 10 min
Strain, sweeten
Serve hot
drinks.description: Tea brewed from coffee cherry husks — older than coffee itself.

drinks.name: Yemeni Coffee
instructions: Brew coffee with cardamom and ginger
Add sugar
Serve in small cups
drinks.description: Spiced Yemeni coffee — from the birthplace of coffee.

drinks.name: Chai Aden (Aden-Style Tea)
ingredients: Black tea (strong -- CTC or dust grade for full extraction)
instructions: Chai Aden is the sweet, spiced, milky tea of Aden -- Yemen's port city
Strong black tea brewed with spices and sweetened heavily
Evaporated or condensed milk gives it a creamy richness
The spice blend: cardamom, cloves, cinnamon -- the Indian Ocean chai connection
Aden's position on the Indian Ocean trade routes brought Indian chai traditions to Yemen
Drunk throughout the day -- at home, at cafes, at work
The tea culture: Yemeni men chew qat (khat) in the afternoon while drinking chai
drinks.description: Aden port city tea -- chai Aden, strong black tea with cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, and evaporated milk, heavily sweetened. Indian Ocean trade brought chai traditions to Yemen's port. Drunk throughout the day. Yemeni men chew qat in the afternoon while drinking chai.

drinks.name: Shahi Haleeb (Royal Milk)
instructions: Shahi haleeb is the Yemeni spiced milk drink -- "royal milk"
Warm milk infused with cardamom and saffron, sweetened with sugar
Garnished with crushed nuts
Drunk warm as an evening or after-dinner drink
The saffron and cardamom: the Arabian luxury flavors
A comforting, soothing nighttime drink
drinks.description: Yemeni spiced milk -- shahi haleeb (royal milk), warm milk infused with cardamom and saffron, sweetened and garnished with crushed almonds or pistachios. A comforting evening drink. Saffron and cardamom are the Arabian luxury flavors.
